lc_person: Lewis Bayly, bishop of Bangor and devotional writer; author of The Practice of Piety.
item_person: Lewis Bayly, bishop of Bangor in 1616–1631 and writer.

evidence.says: Identifies the author of The Practice of Piety; cites Oxford Dictionary of National Biography for the bishop of Bangor, born approximately 1575, died 1631.
Lists birth in 1565, death in 1631, the bishopric of Bangor in 1616–1631, LC n83238533 and Dictionary of Welsh Biography identifier s-BAYL-LEW-1575.
Dictionary of Welsh Biography identifies the bishop and devotional writer, estimates birth around 1575, and explicitly says the birth date is uncertain.

notes: Same name, office and death year. Supported birth is approximate, not an exact year. The graph supplies only the matching cited name.

lc_person: Nicetas Choniates, historian; author of O City of Byzantium, Annals of Niketas Choniates.
item_person: Niketas Choniates, historian, also identified as Nicetas Acominatus.

evidence.says: Cites O City of Byzantium (1984) under Niketas Choniates, and Grandezza e catastrofe di Bisanzio under Niceta Coniata; older Britannica citation supplies approximately 1140–1213.
Identifies the historian Niketas Choniates, gives 1155–1217, and links LC n83319403, BnF 13091715n and ISNI 0000000110261851.
BnF gives birth as 1155? and death as 1216?; lists Niketas Choniates, Nicetas Acominatus Choniates and Niceta Coniate as name forms, with ISNI 0000000110261851 and historical works.

notes: Name forms and works identify the same historian. Prefer approximately 1155, with BnF’s explicit uncertainty; LC retains older dates. The cited-name key provides no independent biographical detail.

lc_person: Henri Dubief, historian and teacher at Lycée Henri-IV; coauthor of La crise des années 30.
item_person: Henri Dubief, historian and secondary-school teacher, linked to BnF 11900762b.

evidence.says: Cites La crise des années 30 (1989), coauthored with Dominique Borne, and teaching at Lycée Henri-IV; its cover-derived note and birth field give 1913.
Gives birth in 1910, occupations historian and teacher, LC n84011008, BnF 11900762b and VIAF 46760298.
BnF identifies the historian and Lycée Henri-IV teacher, cites the same book with Dominique Borne, and gives 1910–1995; its sources include a birth-register entry.
Agulhon and Lalouette’s 1996 scholarly obituary identifies historian Henri Dubief with birth year 1910 and death year 1995, and discusses his historical works.

notes: Matching coauthored book and teaching affiliation establish identity. BnF and the scholarly obituary support 1910 over LC’s book-cover-derived 1913. Graph evidence is the matching cited name only.

lc_person: John Solomos, politics lecturer at Birkbeck; author of Black Youth, Racism and the State.
item_person: John Solomos, politics lecturer at Birkbeck and sociologist, linked to the University of Warwick profile.

evidence.says: Identifies the Birkbeck politics lecturer and author of Black youth, racism, and the state; the source note for Racism and equal opportunity in the 1980s reports a 1955 birth, although the structured birth field says 1950.
Gives birth in 1955; identifies the Birkbeck politics lecturer and sociologist, links LC n84092835 and a Warwick staff profile, and lists ORCID 0000-0003-1274-9310.
John Solomos’s institution-hosted CV gives birth year 1955 and identifies him as Professor of Sociology at Warwick.

notes: LC has an internal date inconsistency: its bibliographic source note agrees with Wikidata and the CV on 1955. Matching name and affiliation support the cited-name key.

lc_person: Robert Baillie, Glasgow minister and author of The Letters and Journals of Robert Baillie.
item_person: Robert Baillie, minister and theologian associated with the University of Glasgow.

evidence.says: Cites The letters and journals of Robert Baillie (1841–1842); heading and DNB citation give 1599–1662, while NUC and an earlier LC heading give 1602–1662.
Gives birth in 1602 and death in 1662, University of Glasgow affiliation, LC n84121391 and VIAF 30601102; also links the older DNB article headed 1599–1662.
Alexander D. Campbell’s 2017 biography states that Baillie was born in 1602; its chapter summary cites Baillie’s own record of his birth in a student notebook.

notes: Same author; LC preserves conflicting historical date traditions. The modern scholarly biography supports 1602. Graph evidence is only the matching cited name.

lc_person: John Frederick Adam Sawyer, linguist and Old Testament scholar; author of Isaiah and The Fifth Gospel.
item_person: John F. A. Sawyer, Hebrew Bible scholar, linked to LC n84144821 and VIAF 76352505.

evidence.says: Cites Isaiah (1984–), The fifth gospel (1996) and Sacred languages and sacred texts (1999); its Scotsman obituary note identifies John Frederick Adam Sawyer, born 1935, died 2022.
Identifies the Hebrew Bible scholar with LC n84144821 and VIAF 76352505; contains competing birth statements for 1938 and 1935, plus death in 2022.
The 2022 obituary identifies John Frederick Adam Sawyer as linguist, Old Testament scholar and teacher, gives 1935–2022, and discusses his Isaiah commentary and The Fifth Gospel.

notes: Full name, field and works agree. The obituary supports 1935; Wikidata already contains that year alongside 1938. The graph’s abbreviated cited name is compatible.

lc_person: Jeffrey Paul von Arx, historian; author of Progress and Pessimism (1985).
item_person: Jeffrey P. von Arx, historian and eighth president of Fairfield University, 2004–2016.

evidence.says: Cites Progress and pessimism (1985) under Jeffrey Paul von Arx; the author data sheet supplies birth year 1947, retained in the heading.
Identifies Jeffrey Paul von Arx as historian and president of Fairfield University in 2004–2016; lists LC n84145056 and VIAF 108615170, but birth year 1944 is sourced to a Wikipedia import.
Fairfield’s university archive identifies its eighth president as author of Progress and Pessimism (1985), establishing the link to LC’s author; this profile gives birth year 1949.

notes: Identity is secure through the same book and university role. Birth remains unresolved: LC’s author data sheet gives 1947, Wikidata gives 1944, and Fairfield’s profile gives 1949. The graph supplies the matching cited name only.

lc_person: Chrestien Le Clercq, missionary and historian; author of Nouvelle relation de la Gaspesie (1691).
item_person: Chrétien Le Clercq, missionary and writing-system inventor, also named Chrestien Leclercq.

evidence.says: Cites Nouvelle relation de la Gaspesie (1691) under Chrestien Le Clercq; approximately 1630–1695 comes from Nouvelle biographie générale, while other cited catalogue headings use floruit dates.
Lists Chrestien Leclercq among aliases, birth in 1641, missionary occupation, LC n84177100, and Dictionary of Canadian Biography identifier le_clercq_chrestien_1.
Dictionary of Canadian Biography identifies Chrestien Le Clercq as missionary and historiographer, born in 1641 and still living in 1700.
Québec’s cultural heritage register identifies the historian and missionary, gives 1641–after 1700, and describes 1641 as the probable birth year.

notes: Same author and name variants. DCB and Québec’s register support 1641 over LC’s older approximate 1630; the register qualifies the birth as probable. Matching cited name fits the key.
